sections.text:
In one of the neighboring villages, Juha's faithful donkey, on which he relied in all his work, died, and Juha was deeply saddened by his loss.

Juha did not have money to buy a new donkey, so he decided to travel to a distant village on foot to look for work that would pay for a new donkey.

Juha packed his few belongings into a small bundle, tied it to his back, and began his arduous walk under the blazing sun.

After walking for several hours straight, Juha felt extremely tired and exhausted, his feet were hurting, and sweat was pouring from his forehead profusely.

Juha sat in the shade of a large tree to rest, and began to remember his dead donkey, which he had carried and relieved him of this torment.

Juha started crying and mourning for his donkey, saying in a loud voice: “Alas, my dear donkey! You died and left me suffering the torment of walking and fatigue! Where are you now to carry me?!”

While he was crying and lamenting his misfortune, a nobleman of the city passed by him riding a thoroughbred horse and behind him a convoy of slaves and servants.

The nobleman heard Juha crying and wailing, so he stopped his horse and looked at him with pity, and asked him: “What is wrong with you, man? Why are you crying so bitterly in the middle of the desert? Have you lost a loved one?”

Juha wanted to take advantage of the situation and arouse the man’s pity, perhaps giving him money or riding with him. He said while wiping his fake tears: “Yes, sir! I have lost the most precious thing I own. My only son and the support I depended on in my life has died, leaving me alone to struggle with the world!”

The nobleman's heart was very moved by Juha's condition, and he ordered his servants to provide him with food and drink, then he took out a bag full of golden dinars and gave him to Juha as compensation for his great loss and to console him for his loss.

Juha was so happy that he could not hide it, so he took the gold and began to pray for goodness and blessings for the nobleman.

Before the nobleman left, he wanted to ask about the cause of death to console him more, so he said: “May God have mercy on your son, my brother.

But tell me, why did your young son die? Was he sick or did he die in an accident?

Juha completely forgot the lie he had told a while ago because of his overwhelming joy over the gold, and he remembered his dead donkey that he had been crying over at the beginning!
Juha answered with complete spontaneity and a sad voice: “No, sir, he was not sick and did not die in an accident.

The poor guy died because he ate too much tough barley and was unable to digest it!

The nobleman stopped moving and looked at Juha in astonishment and shock! Is there a person who dies from eating too much tough barley?!
The nobleman asked with suspicion and anger: “He eats barley?! Is your son a human or an animal?!”

The stupid Juha realized that he had exposed himself with his tongue, and that he had exposed his lie, so he tried to patch up the situation and said in confusion: “I mean, sir.

I mean, he loved barley bread so much!”

But the nobleman was not convinced, and he realized that Juha was deceiving him and crying over a donkey, not over a human being. He became extremely angry and ordered his servants to retrieve the gold immediately, and he severely beat Juha to teach him not to lie and deceive people.

Juha returned, dragging his tired feet, learning a hard lesson that “the rope of lies is short,” and that the fraudster often falls into the trap with his stupidity and tongue.
